title: What a sponge city can do: Basel
purpose: One column per action. Row 1: what is possible, for whom. Row 2: what Basel is already doing (verified, or visibly empty). Row 3: where the potential is, with numbers from open data. Row 4: how to get there (our proposals).

context.new: New development or full street rebuild

evidence.observed: Published by an authority or stated in an official source, quoted as published
evidence.derived: Computed by us from open Basel data; method named; reproducible with scripts/compute_potential.py; for explaining and screening only
evidence.assumed: Our reasoning or a proposal; not measured
evidence.unknown: No open data found in the reviewed Basel and federal sources

basel_status.in-progress: Under construction, being piloted or being planned
basel_status.announced: Announced; depends on a pending decision
basel_status.none-found: Nothing published found in the reviewed sources

city_findings.text: Of about 1,650 ha of sealed ground in Basel-Stadt, 296 ha (18 %) lies on Allmend parcels and 1,353 ha (82 %) on other parcels: 601 ha buildings, 490 ha other paving (courtyards, forecourts, yards, parking, rail and industrial areas) and 262 ha of road surface.
city_findings.method: Each land-cover polygon is assigned to the parcel containing its representative point; Allmend = parcel type 'Allmendparzelle'.
limitations: Polygons crossing parcel boundaries count wholly to one parcel
'Other parcels' include land owned by the canton, municipalities and SBB, not only private owners
Parcel data carries no owner field

city_findings.text: The canton states: "The greatest potential lies in the many large and small private open spaces of our city."
137.7 km of streets rated sponge-suitable by traffic lie in heat areas marked Fokus (77.9 km) or Verbessern (59.8 km).
city_findings.method: Middle vertex of each segment's longest part, tested against the heat focus polygons; lengths from the canton's segment table.
limitations: Traffic is the only suitability criterion; utilities, groundwater and space are not in the rating
One point per segment decides its heat area

city_findings.text: 231 of 334 active or upcoming permitted works (snapshot 3 October 2026) lie within 60 m of those suitable streets in heat areas.
city_findings.method: Permit point within 60 m of the middle vertex of a suitable segment in a Fokus or Verbessern area; upcoming = permit ends October 2026 or later.
limitations: Permits are not a coordinated works plan
60 m is a screening radius, not a design rule

actions.name: Unseal street space
actions.what: Take out asphalt that traffic does not need; replace it with loosened soil and planting.

basel.text: About 1,000 m² unsealed and about 600 m² of new green space at Sevogelstrasse, from spring 2026.
Heat protection on about 30 streets during the district-heating build-out, including unsealing.

potential.text: 296 ha of sealed ground lie on Allmend parcels.
137.7 km of traffic-suitable streets lie in heat areas.

actions.name: Unseal courtyards and forecourts
actions.what: Private and public grounds: replace paving in courtyards, front gardens and yards with planting that takes roof and yard water.

basel.text: A funding programme for unsealing, trees and green spaces on private property, to launch in 2026 if the Grand Council approves it.
The canton offers advice to owners and grants via the value-added levy fund and Swisslos for citizen initiatives.

potential.text: 490 ha of other paving (courtyards, forecourts, yards, parking, rail and industrial land) lie outside Allmend parcels.
The canton itself sees the greatest potential on private open spaces.

actions.name: Keep trees; give them root space
actions.what: Protect existing trees and plant new ones with enough soil volume and planted area around them.

basel.text: About 200 trees planted along streets and in green spaces in 2024.
Engelgasse: tree pits enlarged and 50 young trees planted (2016).
Over 28,000 trees in the cadastre; about 1 % of the stock is renewed each year.

potential.text: 9,132 of 12,504 street-tree points have no mapped planted polygon at the point. This does not mean sealed paving and does not reveal pit size.
Bern's guidance targets 36 m³ of root space per street tree.

actions.name: Tree trench (Baumrigole)
actions.what: A load-bearing root bed under the pavement that also takes street runoff.

basel.text: Sponge-city elements tested in the new VoltaNord streets, with five years of scientific monitoring.
ZHAW develops substrates and vegetation for Therwiler-, Lysbüchel- and Weinlagerstrasse.

potential.text: 231 active or upcoming works lie near traffic-suitable streets in heat areas: moments when the street is open anyway.

actions.name: Rain garden and swale
actions.what: A shallow planted hollow that collects runoff from paving and lets it soak in or evaporate.

basel.text: Vegetated swales and mulch beds that take sidewalk and road runoff, e.g. Sevogelstrasse.

potential.text: At the 81 monitoring stations, the shallowest groundwater level in ten years lies 0.8 m to 20.8 m below ground (median 9.8 m). Stations are points, not a depth map; infiltration needs a site test.

actions.name: Lead road water into green
actions.what: Open the kerb so road runoff reaches a rain garden or tree trench instead of the gully.

basel.text: At Sevogelstrasse, rain from sidewalk and road is to collect and soak in under the new trees.

potential.text: About 507 ha of mapped road surface: 245 ha on Allmend parcels and 262 ha on other parcels.
Where each road drains today is not open data (no sewer or gully data found).

actions.name: Permeable parking
actions.what: Grass-joint stones or open joints let rain soak in where cars stand.

basel.text: Surfaces for depaved parking spaces tested in 2022.
14 grass-joint parking bays at Sevogelstrasse; parking there goes from 36 to 19 spaces.

potential.text: The canton counts about 20,000 blue-zone and about 2,100 paid street parking spaces (counts per street, without geometry).
Bay geometry is not open, so the paved parking area cannot be measured yet.

actions.name: Green roof
actions.what: A planted layer on flat roofs that holds back and evaporates part of the rain.

basel.text: § 72 BPG: flat roofs of 10 m² or more must be greened when built or renovated (at least 15 cm substrate).
Funding for roof greening beyond the minimum, planned from 2026.

potential.text: Buildings cover about 606 ha, 16.6 % of the mapped ground (601 ha of it outside Allmend parcels).
Which roofs are flat, already green or strong enough is not open data.

actions.name: Disconnect downpipes
actions.what: Lead roof water into a garden, swale or barrel instead of the sewer.

basel.text: Rainwater fee of CHF 0.90 per m² of sealed area connected to the sewer.

potential.text: ≈ Because the fee is charged on connected sealed area, disconnecting a roof should lower it; the fee page does not state this rule explicitly.
How roofs drain today (sewer, infiltration) is not open data.

actions.name: Rain barrel or cistern
actions.what: Collect roof water for watering; it helps in storms only if empty beforehand.

basel.text: No Basel programme found.

potential.text: ≈ Small for flooding, useful for watering young trees and gardens in dry summers.

actions.name: Water square
actions.what: A public square that stores water briefly in a cloudburst and is a place to stay when dry.

basel.text: No Basel water square found.

potential.text: Rotterdam's Benthemplein stores about 1,800 m³.
Where Basel's streets pond in cloudbursts is not open (only a modelled national overland-flow map).

actions.name: Keep gullies clear
actions.what: Leaves, litter and sand in gullies cause much local flooding; cleaning is a sponge action too.

basel.text: No published gully-cleaning data found.

potential.text: In two Dutch cities, 70 % of resident flood reports were caused by blocked gully pots, not too little pipe capacity.

actions.name: Dig once
actions.what: When a street is opened for pipes, heating or tracks, rebuild it as a sponge street in the same works.

basel.text: District heating grows by about 60 km by 2037; the canton uses it to redesign streets, about 30 so far; 55 % of these projects hold potential for unsealing and greening.

potential.text: 231 of 334 active or upcoming permits lie near traffic-suitable streets in heat areas.

actions.name: Sponge districts from the start
actions.what: In new districts, plan water paths, storage, parks and trees before the buildings.

basel.text: VoltaNord: sponge-city elements in the new streets, monitored for five years.
Klybeck (almost 30 ha): two parks, green courtyards, facade greening and unsealed surfaces planned; building plan expected early 2027. Rainwater management is not mentioned in the release.

potential.text: ≈ The cheapest moment: water paths and soil volume cost least before buildings and pipes are fixed.

levers.name: Rules
levers.text: Ask for sponge-city requirements (water paths, root space, unsealed share) in every building plan, as Klybeck's plan is being drafted.

levers.name: Dig once by default
levers.text: Check every street permit near a suitable street in a heat area for a sponge rebuild; publish a coordinated multi-year works plan.

levers.name: Money
levers.text: Prioritise the 2026 private greening fund for courtyards in heat areas; state explicitly that disconnected roofs pay a lower rainwater fee.

levers.name: Standards
levers.text: Set a root-space target for every new street tree (Bern uses 36 m³) and a standard for kerb inlets into green.

levers.name: Data
levers.text: Publish gully points and drainage type per street, tree-pit sizes, a green-roof inventory and parking geometry (the Data Charter asks).

levers.name: People
levers.text: Invite residents to water young trees and report blocked gullies; advise owners of large courtyards directly.
